question: Can a continuous-time attention layer expose useful per-query predictive uncertainty in the same deterministic pass that produces its prediction, without an uncertainty head, repeated model evaluations, or a changed training loss?

key_findings.claim: The proposed Poisson-random-measure attention has a deterministic mean path equal to the sampled operator's expectation and an exact closed-form root-mean-square deviation that factorizes into attended-value disagreement and total compatibility evidence.
key_findings.evidence: Theorems 1 and 2 condition on the Poisson atom count: the fallback makes every conditional output mean equal to the mollified cosine-attention output, while conditional sample-mean variance is tr Sigma_V divided by the count; averaging over a Poisson count yields tr Sigma_V times phi(Lambda).

key_findings.claim: The attention swap preserved point-prediction accuracy reasonably well in the matched forecasting backbone, but it was not uniformly free: relative MSE changes were +2.0% on PhysioNet, +5.6% on Activity, and -0.2% on USHCN.
key_findings.evidence: Across five seeds, the matched softmax versus Levy decode MSEs were 5.68 versus 5.80 on PhysioNet (times 10^-3), 2.58 versus 2.73 on Activity (times 10^-3), and 4.65 versus 4.64 on USHCN (times 10^-1).

key_findings.claim: Value disagreement was the robust free error-ranking signal; total evidence helped mainly when observation coverage varied substantially.
key_findings.evidence: In forecasting, evidence-only Spearman correlation was 0.01 on PhysioNet and 0.03 on Activity but 0.40 on sparse USHCN. In five-seed interpolation suites, disagreement achieved AUSE 0.438 versus 0.482 for 20-pass MC dropout on PhysioNet and 0.341 versus 0.560 on USHCN, with the paper reporting a disagreement win in every seed on AUSE in both suites.

key_findings.claim: A validation-calibrated Gaussian using the analytic deviation scale improved probabilistic accuracy over the same model's point prediction and sampled Levy outputs, while split conformal corrected high-level undercoverage.
key_findings.evidence: On PhysioNet interpolation, zero-sample Gaussian CRPS was 0.244, versus 0.317 for the deterministic point law and 0.262 for 50 Levy draws. Gaussian coverage was 80.2%, 87.1%, and 90.8% at nominal 80%, 90%, and 95%; split-conformal coverage was 80.8%, 90.6%, and 95.3%, with greater interval width.

key_findings.claim: Single-pass disagreement enabled cohort-scale trust ranking with similar worst-decile concentration to MC dropout at much lower measured latency.
key_findings.evidence: On 3,383 untouched PhysioNet set-b records and 373,713 hidden-target queries, one pass took 1.35 seconds and concentrated 29.9% excess error in the least-trusted decile; 20-pass dropout took 18.5 seconds and concentrated 29.6%. The dense 35,074,944-query pass took 6.8 seconds versus 133.5 seconds for dropout.

key_findings.claim: The learned channel coordinate is important: a time-only index mixes co-temporal variables and materially damages interpolation accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: In the one-seed geometry ablation, time-only grids produced MAE 0.386, 0.371, and 0.365, whereas the 16-by-8 time-by-learned-channel grid produced 0.302 and sat 1.5% from its matched softmax control.

method.core_idea: Replace one cross-attention layer with a compound-Poisson integral over a continuous time-by-channel index space, but train and normally infer through its exact deterministic expectation.
method.mechanism: Cosine query-key compatibility defines an unnormalized intensity. Keys deposit normalized Gaussian bumps on a fixed grid; an RBF-interpolated value field supplies values at grid cells. Total intensity Lambda is evidence, value covariance under normalized intensity is disagreement, and their exact combination sqrt(tr Sigma_V times phi(Lambda)) is the sampled layer's RMS deviation. Optional samples redraw only Poisson cell counts while reusing the encoder, intensity, and value field.
assumptions: The intensity is positive and evidence is well above the low-count regime where phi(Lambda) is non-monotone; all reported experiments satisfy this empirically.
The layer's internal deviation is informative about target error after a global validation calibration; the theory does not establish this transfer.
Split-conformal coverage requires exchangeable calibration and test queries.
The fixed grid and mollifier provide an acceptable coarse-grained substitute for discrete softmax attention.

techniques.role: Turns unnormalized compatibility mass into an atom count and gives the stochastic operator analytically tractable moments.
Separates uncertainty into attended-value disagreement and an inverse-evidence count factor without sampling.
Substitutes the exact operator mean during training, avoiding stochastic-gradient variance and a train-inference gap.
Defines a convex value field at arbitrary continuous locations while preserving per-key mass at boundaries.
Reuses the expensive encoder, kernel, intensity, and value field when optional output samples are requested.
Maps layer-space deviation to scalar target scale with one global affine fit before Gaussian or conformal intervals are formed.

evaluations.setting: t-PatchGNN-protocol forecasting on PhysioNet 2012, Human Activity, and USHCN; five seeds; matched approximately 0.7M-parameter backbone.
evaluations.metric: Test MSE, with dataset-specific table scaling.
evaluations.baseline: Matched softmax decode: 5.68 +/- 0.27, 2.58 +/- 0.02, and 4.65 +/- 0.06 on the same scales.

evaluations.setting: PhysioNet 2012 interpolation with 30% masking; five matched seeds.
evaluations.metric: AUSE for per-query absolute-error ranking; lower is better.
evaluations.baseline: 20-pass MC dropout: 0.482 +/- 0.009; post-hoc variance head: 0.441 +/- 0.023; Gaussian-NLL head: 0.242 +/- 0.013 but with 14.1% +/- 5.1% worse MAE.

evaluations.setting: Sparse USHCN interpolation with 30% masking; five matched seeds.
evaluations.metric: Spearman rho / AUSE for per-query error ranking.

evaluations.setting: PhysioNet interpolation probabilistic prediction at 30% masking; five seeds for CRPS and one checkpoint for coverage.
evaluations.metric: Validation-calibrated CRPS and empirical interval coverage.
evaluations.result: Zero-sample Gaussian on analytic deviation: CRPS 0.244 +/- 0.006; split-conformal coverage 80.8%, 90.6%, and 95.3% at nominal 80%, 90%, and 95%.
evaluations.baseline: Same model as point prediction: CRPS 0.317 +/- 0.007; 50 Levy draws: 0.262 on one seed; five-model ensemble: 0.229 +/- 0.005.

evaluations.setting: Untouched PhysioNet set-b cohort of 3,383 records on one RTX 3090, with quality averaged over five trainings.
evaluations.metric: Wall-clock, patient-level Spearman rho, and excess MAE in flagged worst decile.
evaluations.result: One-pass disagreement: 1.35 seconds, rho 0.43 +/- 0.08, flagged-decile excess error +29.9% +/- 2.8%.

limitations: Author-stated: the identities certify sampling deviation of one attention layer, not predictive error; target-error usefulness is empirical.
Author-stated: evidence is uninformative on dense coverage, free signals rank Activity errors poorly, and sparse-USHCN evidence varies substantially by seed.
Author-stated: Gaussian tails under-cover at high nominal levels, while conformal validity depends on exchangeability and therefore does not survive arbitrary distribution shift.
Author-stated: the predictive scale needs validation calibration because the analytic statistic is a vector-layer deviation rather than the scalar head's deviation.
Author-stated: experiments cover one decoder layer, three public irregular-time-series benchmarks, backbones no larger than 20.3M parameters, and several single-seed ablations.
Reviewer inference: 'zero marginal cost' excludes the retraining and possible accuracy loss required by the operator transplant, as well as the added grid computation inside the replaced layer.
failure_modes: When nearby compatible values agree but the downstream head is wrong for representation or distribution-shift reasons, disagreement can be low despite large target error.
When evidence enters the very-low-count regime, the empty-draw fallback makes phi(Lambda) non-monotone, so the usual less-evidence-means-more-deviation reading fails.
Dense datasets suppress evidence variation; combining its factor with disagreement can worsen ranking relative to disagreement alone.
A coarse time-only grid blends variables observed at the same timestamp and damages accuracy; inadequate learned channel separation can recreate this failure.
Global affine calibration can miss variable-specific scales, nonlinear heads, heavy tails, or deployment shift.
reusable_insights: Before normalizing any attention or kernel row, retain its partition function as a coverage diagnostic instead of discarding it.
Pair evidence with the weighted dispersion of values: count or density alone cannot distinguish many identical observations from many conflicting ones.
If a stochastic module has tractable conditional moments, train through its exact expectation and expose analytic moments in the default deterministic pass.
Separate uncertainty ranking from interval scaling; the best triage score need not be the statistic with the right physical units for calibration.
For irregular multivariate data, a learned auxiliary coordinate can stop continuous interpolation from averaging semantically different co-temporal channels.
open_questions: Does the disagreement-over-evidence decomposition remain useful in large transformer blocks, self-attention, or multimodal attention rather than a single continuous-time decoder layer?
Can the layer-space variance be propagated analytically through a nonlinear prediction head, removing the global validation scale fit?
Would variable-conditional or locally adaptive calibration improve tail coverage without sacrificing the zero-sample advantage?
How robust are evidence and disagreement under covariate, temporal, and clinical site shift?
Can grid-free quadrature or adaptive cells preserve the identities while reducing the operator's constant-factor cost?

competitive_landscape.title: Multi-Time Attention Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series
competitive_landscape.difference: mTAN uses deterministic continuous-time attention to build irregular-series representations, whereas LevyAttention replaces the attention operator with a Poisson construction whose partition mass and value covariance yield analytic per-query uncertainty.

competitive_landscape.title: Bayesian Attention Modules
competitive_landscape.difference: Bayesian Attention Modules learn and repeatedly sample reparameterizable attention distributions, whereas LevyAttention trains through an exact deterministic mean and emits its second moment before any sample is drawn.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformer Neural Processes: Uncertainty-Aware Meta Learning Via Sequence Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: Transformer Neural Processes learn a native predictive distribution with a probabilistic sequence-model objective, whereas LevyAttention retrofits one attention layer and derives operator uncertainty without changing the supervised point-prediction loss.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first attention-native, closed-form single-pass uncertainty interface based on a Poisson random measure, with an exact disagreement-over-evidence variance identity.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The construction, mean and variance proofs, matched softmax transplant, frozen-model estimator suite, calibration tests, and cohort timing jointly support that this is more than a renamed confidence head or repeated stochastic attention scheme.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the exact moment identity tied to quantities already computed by unnormalized attention. The broader claim that useful predictive uncertainty is free should be read narrowly: it is empirically strong on two interpolation regimes but uneven on Activity, needs retraining and calibration, and competes with simple post-hoc heads when labels are available.

reviewer_notes: Full text and appendices were read. Quantitative statements were checked against Tables 1, 3-6, 8, and 9 and the cited prose. Author claims and reviewer inference are labeled explicitly; comparisons to prior work use primary arXiv records.
